why: MATLAB runs a script's statements in order (the user's ruling 3, text order in a script; doc 'clear'): a clear removes the names it matches where it stands, and an assignment after it makes the name again. `clear xa*` then `xa1 = 5`, `clear xb` then `xb = 5`, `clearvars -except qq` then `xc = 5`, `clear -regexp ^xd` then `xd = 5` each leave the name in the caller's workspace, so the caller's read of it indexes the variable (a dormant row, no call out of the index); `xa2 = 5` then `clear xa*` leaves none (a failed row).
